headline: Choose, recurse, and undo
statement: Return every possible ordering of nums, whose values are distinct. Any ordering of the result list is accepted.
intuition: A permutation puts all the numbers in an order. Build that order one position at a time by choosing any number not already used. After exploring a choice, remove it so another choice can use that position. Save a copy when the order contains every number.
approach: Maintain path and used while recursively constructing positions.
Choose each unused value and recurse.
When path has n values, save a copy; afterward undo each choice.
correctness: Each recursion depth assigns exactly one position, and used prevents repeated values. Every permutation has a unique sequence of choices, so it is reached once. The backtracking restoration ensures no branch inherits another branch’s choices.
bruteForce: Generate n^n length-n sequences and discard those with repeated values; this examines far more invalid candidates.

complexity.explanation: There are n! answers, each copied in O(n); recursion and current path have depth n.

pitfalls: Append a copy of path, not the shared path object.
Remove both the chosen value and its used marker when backtracking.
Output order is unrestricted, but duplicate or missing permutations are invalid.
